headline: Gold prices jump 4,374 TK per bhori; 22K gold now 234,038 TK
summary: The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) has increased gold prices for the second day in a row, marking the 100th price adjustment of the year.
details: The price of 22-carat gold has risen by 4,374 TK per bhori, bringing the new price to 234,038 TK, according to a notice from the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) on Saturday.
// New prices are effective from 10 AM on August 8. 21-carat gold is now 223,541 TK, 18-carat gold is 191,931 TK, and traditional method gold is 156,823 TK per bhori.
caption:
Gold prices surge again! 22K gold hits 234,038 TK per bhori after a 4,374 TK jump.

The price of 22-carat gold has risen by 4,374 TK per bhori, bringing the new price to 234,038 TK, according to a notice from the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (BAJUS) on Saturday.

// New prices are effective from 10 AM on August 8. 21-carat gold is now 223,541 TK, 18-carat gold is 191,931 TK, and traditional method gold is 156,823 TK per bhori.

headline: 54 all out: Bangladesh suffer innings defeat in warm-up vs CA XI
summary: The Tigers are bowled out for just 54 in their second innings, raising concerns over batting form ahead of the Test series against Australia.
details: Bangladesh suffered a crushing innings-and-38-run defeat against Cricket Australia XI in a three-day warm-up game in Darwin.
The visitors were bowled out for just 54 in their second innings, adding only 35 runs to their overnight score of 19 for two.
Cricket Australia XI had previously established a 92-run first-innings lead, scoring 355 in response to Bangladesh's 263.
Tanzid Tamim top-scored with 22 off 41 balls, while ten batters fell for single-digit scores across the match's final stages.
Campbell Thompson dominated the bowling for CA XI, taking eight wickets for 25 runs in 11 overs.
Despite the loss, national team physio Bayjedul Islam confirmed that Taijul Islam's finger injury has improved significantly.
The physio expressed confidence that the left-arm spinner will be fit and available for the first Test match.
The first Test begins in Darwin on August 13, with the second match scheduled for Mackay on August 22.
caption:
Bowled out for 54! 🏏

Bangladesh suffers a heavy innings defeat in their final warm-up game before the Test series.

Bangladesh suffered a crushing innings-and-38-run defeat against Cricket Australia XI in a three-day warm-up game in Darwin.

The visitors were bowled out for just 54 in their second innings, adding only 35 runs to their overnight score of 19 for two.

Cricket Australia XI had previously established a 92-run first-innings lead, scoring 355 in response to Bangladesh's 263.

Tanzid Tamim top-scored with 22 off 41 balls, while ten batters fell for single-digit scores across the match's final stages.

Campbell Thompson dominated the bowling for CA XI, taking eight wickets for 25 runs in 11 overs.

Despite the loss, national team physio Bayjedul Islam confirmed that Taijul Islam's finger injury has improved significantly.

The physio expressed confidence that the left-arm spinner will be fit and available for the first Test match.

The first Test begins in Darwin on August 13, with the second match scheduled for Mackay on August 22.
